messages:
olivia: Thinking out loud — would be great to add a "Threshold Calibration" wizard in the console that ingests recent telemetry and suggests per-route SLO thresholds and expected alert volume. It could give a preview of noise vs sensitivity. cc @matt @shawn

matt: love the idea. main question: should the wizard call an internal /calibrate API or run client-side in the console using sampled telemetry? Server-side gives more data but needs feature-flag rollout and quota controls. :thinking:

shawn: server-side preferred for accurate percentiles. We already have the metrics pipeline to compute p50/p95/p99 per-tenant per-route. downside: compute cost and retention windows. Could do 7/30/90 day options.

olivia: Agreed. UX: show a slider for alert aggressiveness (conservative <-> aggressive) and a small estimate: "estimated alerts/day". Also allow export of the chosen threshold to an API patch for the route.

sara: UX nit — preview should also show historical false positives (alerts that suppressed by known quiet windows). Otherwise customers will think calibration is broken. Maybe a toggle for "exclude scheduled maintenance".

matt: API debate: two options — POST /routes/{id}/calibrate which returns suggestions but doesn't persist, or a dry-run + PATCH to persist. I prefer explicit persist flow: POST -> UI preview -> PATCH if user confirms. Keeps API idempotent.

jessica: +1 on explicit persist. Also we should surface an "expected cost delta" (compute + alerting noise) in the wizard. Finance folks ask for that.

shawn: telemetry detail: we need per-token latency buckets and error-cause tags to avoid tuning on transient client errors. Example logs we should ignore: 5xx from downstream, rate-limit spikes, internal deployments.

olivia: Good call. Add a checkbox: "ignore deploy windows" that maps to a filter against deploy metadata.

matt: Implementation sketch (pseudo payload):

```json
POST /api/v1/routes/123/calibrate
{
  "lookback_days": 30,
  "percentiles": [95, 99],
  "exclude_labels": ["deploy", "maintenance"],
  "aggressiveness": 0.6
}
```

Response: suggestion list with threshold, expected alert rate, confidence score.

sara: For the console, show a small inline sparkline with annotated examples where the recommended threshold would have fired in the past 30d. That helps trust.

olivia: UX question: should the wizard propose separate thresholds per severity (p1/p2) or just one threshold and let customers map actions?

matt: I think single threshold per route + optional per-notification-level overrides. Keep it simple initially.

jessica: Can we add a telemetry toggle to compute "alert fusion" — if multiple routes would have triggered same incident, show de-duplicated alert count. That should reduce perceived noise in the preview.

shawn: On storage: computing calibration in real-time is expensive. Suggest we run a nightly job that populates a calibration cache per-tenant, and the API reads the cache with a strong cache TTL but supports manual refresh.

deploy-bot: feature-flag created: ff/threshold-calibration-wizard (owner: olivia).

olivia: Thanks bot. Next steps: shawn and infra to sketch the calibration job and required metrics, matt to draft the API schema and confirm PATCH/POST semantics, sara to prototype the UI flow, jessica to add cost delta fields to the bill-of-materials. I'll put a PR template in the design doc.

matt: One more thought — allow customers to run calibration in "dry-run" mode for a week to collect real alert impressions before persisting. Could be a paid feature for Dedicated/Private?

jessica: Worth flagging to product. I'll add it to the feature brief.

sara: I'll mock the modal tomorrow and include a compact preview card for the console route list.

shawn: I'll prototype the nightly job and share ops hygiene (backfills, retention). Expect a quick spike if we enable 90-day windows.

olivia: Great. If nobody objects, I'll open a tracking issue and tag folks. :thumbsup:

matt: go for it.

jessica: go for it.

sara: +1

shawn: +1
